note: The game controller singleton. Created by java.game.Init's constructor (`gameLogic = new GameLogic()`), runs from there on: `createNativeInstance()` in its own constructor, then rpkScan/openLib of the content archives, VehicleType/Chassis/Map scans, controller join loop, `Hotkey`s for music/screenshot, a clock Thread, and finally `changeActiveSection(new SplashScreen(frontend.rpk:0x5))`. It is a GameType AND a Runnable whose run() is STATIC.

`GameLogic.kismajomCheck(String[] codes)`: Garage calls it after Input.flushKeys() with the 5 cheat words stored Caesar-shifted by +1 ("mfunfspd" = letmeroc, "cfhgpsnpofz" = begformoney, "gbtuqspnpujpo" = fastpromotion, "jmjlfdifbujoh" = ilikecheating, "ujnfnbdijof" = timemachine). Returns the index of the code the player typed since the last flush, or -1. Effects (Garage.osdCommand CMD_TUNE): 0 ROC start, 1 +100000 money, 2 club promotion, 3 GameLogic.cheats=1, 4 day=180.

A car as a whole: wraps `chassis` (the root Part) and is itself a GameType/GameRef of the native car object (cfg kind `car`). Constructed either from an existing chassis (`Vehicle(Part)`, `set(chassis)`) or by spawning a new one (`Vehicle(GameRef parent, int typeId, int colorIdx, float power, float optical, ...)` which calls `create(parent, new GameRef(typeId), "0,0,0,0,0,0", "Vehicle")`). Settings reach the native car only through EVENT_COMMAND strings: `transmission N`, `steerhelp F`, `asr F`, `abs F`, `difflock F`, `cruise N`, `damage_multiplier F`, `wakeup`.
Squared speed of the car (Valocity treats < 0.25 as stopped; Track displays `sqrt(v)*0.08`). Units not confirmed.
Non-zero while the horn is sounding (City reads it to trigger pedestrian/police reactions).
Float 'crime' level of the car (City multiplies by 1.1 for the police pursuit trigger).
Paint/decal tool state machine (GameState + GameType). Calls the three natives with the clicked part and brush parameters; registers a per-frame `control(float)` callback to paint under the cursor.

`doPaint(GameRef targetPart, int colorARGB, int brushResId, int commit, float rotation, float size, int flip)`: decal/stroke at the cursor pick. `commit`=0 preview (the 'cursor' ghost is passed as target when previewing), 1 apply. Colors are ARGB ints with alpha (`paintColor | 1711276032` = alpha 0x66).
`paintPart(GameRef part, int colorARGB)`: flood-paints a part (alpha forced to 0xFF with `| -16777216`).
`xPaint(GameRef car)`: Painter calls it with player.car (undo/clear paint; exact effect unknown).

Base of every installable part; a GameType created from a gametype entry whose cfg kind is `part` (1,502 of them). Its constructor is `Part(int id)` and chains `super(id)`. The cfg (`slot`/`attach`/`compatible`/`category`...) is parsed by the engine; the script holds the economics (name, value, wear limits, prestige), the install checks and the data the physics reads (see the field contract on the Chassis class). See entry-points.md for the slot protocol.
Float condition factor in [0,1]; 1.0 = new. Repair raises it to repair_max_wear (0.9). 24 sites.
Sets wear; returns float (previous value probably). Part.repair: `if (getWear() < repair_max_wear) setWear(repair_max_wear)`.
Second condition factor (damage/tear), same convention. Part.getConditionNoAttach = wear * tear.
Sets tear.
Lifespan: `setMaxWear(kmToMaxWear(210000))` where kmToMaxWear(km) = km*1000 (metres). Wear accumulates natively with distance driven; 452 name-only sites (every engine/tyre/brake constructor).

Index (0..3 = FL, FR, RL, RR) of the wheel position a suspension/brake/spring part belongs to, derived from the slot it is plugged into. 205 typed sites in the MrSir/CMS suspension scripts.

`disableSlot(int slotId, int disabled)`: 1 greys out/blocks a slot so nothing can be installed or removed there (Chassis.updatevariables enforces an outside-in order this way: while the wheel is fitted only the wheel slot stays enabled, then brake, then spring/shock, then suspension; engine blocks disable crankshaft/camshaft slots).
Per-slot damage state as a String (opaque engine text, saved verbatim by Part.save).
Restores it in Part.load.
`setSlotPos(slotId, Vector3 pos, Ypr ori)`: moves a slot's mount point at runtime (suspension scripts reposition wheel/brake/shock slots: `(101+i)`, `(111+i)`; 328 name-only sites).
Number of slots this part has (cfg `slot` lines).

`getSlotID(index)` -> the slot id declared in the cfg `slot ... <id>` line at that index. `getSlotID(-1)` is used by Part.save as the id of the slot that connects to the parent (it is skipped when saving children).

`partOnSlot(slotId)` -> the child Part script object linked at that slot (null when empty), seen from the part that owns the slot. 150 typed sites. On a child's own mounting slot it yields the parent.

`slotIDOnSlot(slotId)` -> the slot id on the OPPOSITE side of the link that occupies this part's slot `slotId` (0 = empty): Part.save stores it per child; Vehicle.isTestable checks `seat.slotIDOnSlot(1) == 901` (the seat's own mounting slot 1 is plugged into chassis slot 901).

Native dyno/engine-state record (Native subclass). Script-created: `<init>() { super(); newNative(); }`, finalize -> deleteNative.
